## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical iOS basics: SwiftUI data flow, SQLite persistence with GRDB, and accessibility concerns. It also touches migrations and basic testing, which beginners can implement with guidance.

## Key Concepts

- SwiftUI data binding and state management
- GRDB/SQLite data persistence and migrations
- Searchable lists and date filtering
- Accessibility: Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high-contrast
- Lightweight unit/UI testing strategies

## Code Example

```swift
struct Note: Identifiable {
  let id: UUID
  var title: String
  var body: String
  var date: Date
}

func notesForQuery(_ query: String, in notes: [Note]) -> [Note] {
  let q = query.lowercased()
  return notes.filter { $0.title.lowercased().contains(q) || $0.body.lowercased().contains(q) }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you implement migrations and versioning in GRDB for evolving schemas?
- How would you optimize search performance for large note datasets on-device?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question probes security, offline resilience, and real-time media flows on iOS, plus privacy-preserving transcription and CRDT-like consistency.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end screen frame encryption with per-frame keys using CryptoKit
- WebRTC data channels with relay fallback
- On-device Speech framework for privacy-preserving captions
- Offline-first event log with CRDT-like convergence for whiteboard edits
- Crash-safe resume via persistent logs and state snapshots in SQLite/Realm

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal Swift-like pseudocode for frame encryption (note: labeled as javascript per formatting rules)
import CryptoKit
func encryptFrame(_ data: Data, key: SymmetricKey) -> Data? {
  if let sealed = try? AES.GCM.seal(data, using: key) {
    return sealed.combined
  }
  return nil
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test latency bounds under network churn?
- How to rotate keys without breaking decryption mid-stream?
